parsed.explanation: Little documented hostility in ordinary/tourist contact and no criminalisation of trans expression, with courts delivering bathroom and surgical-requirement rulings, offset reserved attitudes, no anti-discrimination/violence statute, gender-segregated baths, and custody by family-register sex with documented 2024-25 mistreatment. Combined regime is protective in civil society but thin in statute and custody; visitor arrest is not documented, so severity is conditional.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No source on passport/visa marker checks; foreign-resident gender change via nationality reported to immigration, with one 2018 ward-office refusal.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented for visitors. Resident conflict-of-laws route exists but described as capable of bureaucratic breakdown.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch could interact with local offices/custody register, but visitor entry practice is not documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Custody follows family-register sex; trans man held in women's prison despite identifying as man (2023); activist held >100 days among men, initially denied hormones, mocked, shower separate only on request (2024-25).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Bar association pressed prison for years and issued warning; hormone later allowed on doctor recommendation. No national housing policy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention for an unrelated matter would expose visitor to birth-sex placement and hormone interruption; no documented arrest for being trans.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Bathing facilities gender-segregated; onsen/sento/super-sento documented difficulty for trans/non-binary visitors. No law permitting or barring access documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Highest court July 2023: ministry violated public-service law barring trans woman from women's workplace bathroom; 2019 damages award. Private/LGBTQ-friendly baths listed as workarounds.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Workplace protection shows courts can remedy facility exclusion, but bathhouse access remains venue-level discretion, not statutory right.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors. Hormone initially denied in detention until doctor recommended it.
care_services.protection: Not documented for visitor care continuity. 2009 discrimination report is dated baseline, not current evidence.
care_services.interaction: Documented hormone denial was in custody, not clinic; visitor clinic access not assessed.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2023 Promotion Act is symbolic/government-duty only, no individual anti-discrimination or violence-protection guarantee; watered down in culture-war debate.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Two pro-trans highest-court decisions and surgery-requirement held unconstitutional show litigation route working; no trans-specific criminal offence documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Weak statute plus strong courts = protection via litigation, not enforceable general right against private parties (unresolved).

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No evidence on minors, family travel, or age-dependent rules.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Little direct hostility in ordinary contact, especially tourist destinations; attitudes reserved, visibility limited. No trans killing/violence figure or police targeting documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented failure to protect; courts awarding damages signal institutional recourse, but street-level police response to trans victims not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reserved attitudes suggest friction more than hostility; absence of violence data is not proof of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statute guaranteeing protection on gender identity; remedies depend on litigation and local negotiation, slow and case-specific.
remedies_unknowns.protection: District 2019 and highest-court 2023 bathroom rulings with damages; bar warning in prison case. Functioning courts documented working for claimants.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies mitigate documented harms where pursued, but visitor short stay and no general statute limit practical use; many unknowns explicitly listed.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: bureaucratic/document friction and reserved attitudes with courts reliably ordering relief and no imprisonment for identity. Here no documented brief detention of visitor and stronger tourist-area tolerance, so slightly higher than 0.65.

Similar in that detention/secondary screening is not the documented pattern and remedies exist, but 0.75-C has recognised passport markers and tribunal access; here entry is not_documented and no anti-discrimination statute, so lower.

Higher than 0.55-C: ward placement/bathhouse segregation causes distress and partial denial, but no documented rule assigning hospital wards by document marker for visitors and bathroom exclusion was ruled unlawful, so exposure is less systematic.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: reserved but low-hostility street environment and functioning courts (bathroom/surgery rulings) protect visitors in ordinary life, while absence of anti-discrimination law, segregated baths, and family-register custody create conditional exposures. Custody mistreatment is documented and severe if detained, but no visitor arrest, entry screening, police targeting, or trans criminalisation is documented. Net is Reduced Risk, below jurisdictions with statutory protections, above those with universal bans or detention for identity.
